plan.disposition: medium+ only rule (SKILL.md Phase Matrix): external plan/iterate review runs only at medium+ complexity; this run is classified small (no risk flags at Stage 2 Repo Scout time) per .shipwright/agent_docs/iterates/iterate-2026-09-06-triage-cross-tree-pending-delivery.plan.json

findings.finding: _emit_json call site and dead None defaults on the two branch-map params.
findings.suggestion: Wrapped the call; dropped the None defaults on the private helper (now keyword-only, required).

findings.finding: _CACHE keyed on path alone while _cached_records now has a keep predicate; safety rests on an undocumented structural invariant (a root's .git cannot be both a directory and a file, so a path can never be read both filtered and unfiltered).
findings.suggestion: Documented the structural reason directly in _cached_records's docstring.

findings.finding: originBranch (per-row) can be ambiguous when a row's pendingStatusDelivery and pendingAmendDelivery come from different branches -- the row flag cannot say which fact it belongs to.
findings.suggestion: Added one sentence to the originBranch paragraph pointing a consumer that needs to disambiguate at the two envelope maps instead.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: The module docstring's caching design is calibrated against '~45 small files'. — Measured the real store: 84 sibling worktrees, some logs 1000+ records with multi-KB fields, e.g. a ~4KB amend detail blob -- not ~45 small files. Every read of a sibling parses and (pre-fix) retained ALL of that per process, on the polled list surface.
findings.suggestion: Filter foreign records to status/amend only before they enter the cache, since nothing downstream ever consumes a foreign append. Fixed: foreign_records_by_branch now passes keep=_is_status_or_amend to _cached_records.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: originBranches names, per id, which branch holds a decision -- correctly, for both the status and amend envelope blocks. — Constructed a two-sibling case: branch A holds a foreign amend for id X, branch B holds a foreign status for id X. {**cross_amends, **cross_status} collapses to one map naming branch B for both, so undeliveredAmends.originBranches reports B, which holds no amend for X -- an actively wrong branch name, not merely a missing one.
findings.suggestion: Thread two separate maps instead of merging. Fixed: cross_tree_delivery_facts now returns (status_ids, amend_ids, status_origin_branches, amend_origin_branches); build_listing uses each only for its own envelope block; a new test reconstructs the two-branch scenario and asserts they stay separate.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: A pending-decision marker naming a branch is always actionable signal. — This repo has ~84 sibling worktrees including clearly abandoned checkouts (superseded -redo/-w3 variants, a fix-main-<sha> throwaway). Since the module never shells out to git, it cannot ask whether a branch is merged or abandoned -- a decision on a dead branch reports pending forever, diluting the 5-id-capped notice with entries an operator can never act on except by deleting the worktree.
findings.suggestion: Document as an accepted design constraint rather than fix -- answering 'is this merged' needs the git subprocess this module deliberately avoids, or a persistent cross-process registry, both out of scope for this fix. Done: added a 'No expiry, by design constraint' paragraph to the module docstring.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: corruption in the JSON contract reports every span that could not be read, so an operator never mistakes an unreadable item for an absent one. — A corrupt span in a SIBLING log goes through report_corruption (stderr only); list --json's corruption block is built from store_facts, which reads only this tree's own tracked+outbox. A decision lost to corruption in a sibling is therefore invisible to the machine contract entirely, with only an indistinguishable stderr basename as a human signal.
findings.suggestion: Fold foreign corruption into the corruption envelope block, or document the gap. Documented (not fixed, to avoid touching the JSON shape itself in this change): added a 'Foreign corruption is stderr-only' paragraph to the module docstring.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: Reading a sibling's tracked log while another process concurrently removes that worktree (git worktree remove) cannot produce a crash or a wrong-branch attribution. — Walked every step of sibling_worktree_logs -> _branch_name -> _cached_records against git worktree remove's actual filesystem sequence (dir delete, then admin-dir prune). Every intermediate OSError path returns None/[]/skip -- could not construct a crash or a wrong attribution; admin-dir reuse is also blocked since git refuses an occupied .git/worktrees/<name> and removal changes .worktrees' own mtime, invalidating the discovery cache.
findings.suggestion: No change needed -- disproof attempt held; every failure path fails toward the safe direction (skip, never crash or mis-attribute).

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: The (path, mtime) cache can never produce a false 'delivered' reading for a LOCAL tracked/outbox file read through _cached_records within cross_tree_delivery_facts. — On a coarse-mtime filesystem, a stale local cache entry could in theory drop a just-appended id from the appended-ids set, silently suppressing a foreign status event that should read pending -- the false-reassurance direction. Not reachable today only because cross_tree_delivery_facts has exactly one call site per process and nothing writes to those files first in the same process.
findings.suggestion: Document the invariant so a future second call site does not silently reintroduce the risk. Done: noted in _cached_records's docstring as part of the structural-safety argument added in this round.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: _branch_name correctly resolves a linked worktree's admin directory from its .git file's gitdir: line on every git worktree layout. — git >= 2.48 with worktree.useRelativePaths can write a RELATIVE gitdir: target. Path(line.split(':',1)[1].strip()) then resolves against the process CWD, not the worktree's own directory -- every sibling's HEAD read fails at once, a total silent regression back to the pre-fix bug with zero error signal. Windows absolute-path parsing (drive letter, forward slashes) was checked against real artifacts on this host and is correct as written.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a non-absolute admin_dir against worktree_dir. Fixed: added the is_absolute() check and resolution; new test uses a genuinely relative path that only resolves correctly from that base.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: The module fixes the general statement in its own docstring: 'a decision recorded in ANY tree other than the one being read is invisible to that reader.' — Only one direction is implemented -- main reads siblings. A worktree still cannot see a decision recorded on main or on a peer worktree, and hooks/iterate phases running inside a worktree are exactly the readers most likely to need that answer. The original docstring stated the general problem without scoping which direction was actually addressed.
findings.suggestion: Scope the docstring's claim to what is implemented and record why the reverse direction is out of scope. Done: docstring now says the fix addresses main-reads-siblings only, and why.

external_code.disposition: external_review.py --mode iterate is gated to medium+ complexity per SKILL.md's Phase Matrix; this run is classified small, so no external code review was due — not a session-policy opt-out
